headline: High: Dify can ingest and act on Authelia-authenticated flows, creating default data-leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes ForwardAuth and OAuth/OIDC, while Dify wires tools into agent/workflow apps and can read uploaded knowledge-base files. No direct shared channel is documented, so the bridge is indirect and likely requires manual copy or workflow wiring. That makes prompt injection plausible but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF Authelia-authenticated content is copied into Dify prompts or knowledge-base files
IF a Dify workflow treats uploaded text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of auth-gated pages into prompts
Add a provenance banner to all imported text
Require human review before promoting uploaded files into agent context
Restrict Dify workflows to allowlisted templates

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles OIDC/OAuth flows, while Dify reads filesystem uploads, stores conversation logs, and handles model-provider API keys and tool credentials. The pair can therefore move sensitive auth or KB content into Dify’s backend in default deployments, creating a realistic leakage path even though no PHI is stated.
conditions: IF Authelia-protected content is forwarded into Dify knowledge-base uploads or agent prompts
IF Dify conversation logs retain that content beyond the intended retention window
mitigations: Minimize sensitive claims in forwarded auth responses
Turn off or shorten Dify conversation-log retention
Separate auth and KB environments by tenant
Redact secrets before upload to Dify
Review provider/tool credential scopes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make broad network calls, and Dify can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, read/write filesystem, and run server-side code in a per-conversation session. Even without modify_git_state, both can mutate shared resources if deployed against the same workspace or backend, so overlapping write authority is credible in default self-hosted setups.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same filesystem or datastore
IF Dify code tools are allowed to write artifacts that Authelia-linked workflows also consume
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate container volume
Disable write access for Dify code tools where possible
Use per-agent service accounts
Add file-locking or queue-based coordination
Keep shared state read-only

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can gate access via ForwardAuth/OIDC, and Dify’s agent/workflow tooling can act on model outputs and user-defined OpenAPI tools. If Authelia-derived claims or tokens are fed into Dify without verification, Dify may propagate mistaken identity or authorization facts into downstream actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF Dify uses Authelia-derived identity or authorization claims as authoritative input
IF a Dify workflow triggers external tools based on those claims without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking tool
Pass only minimal identity claims from Authelia
Log and review all tool-triggering prompts
Require human approval for irreversible actions
Use signed assertions instead of free-text claims

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia and Dify are both open-source and docs-only here, but Dify explicitly stores conversation logs and knowledge-base files while Authelia is an auth layer with broad egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to retention and logging gaps rather than a proven breach class.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Dify conversation logs or uploaded knowledge-base files
IF retention settings are longer than the organization’s policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Dify uploads
Set the shortest feasible log retention
Document data-flow ownership
Review vendor residency and DPA terms
Purge stale conversation logs
